title: Delhi Police Flags Pakistani Social Media Handles Targeting India's NEET Protests
excerpt: Authorities say hundreds of accounts previously active during Operation Sindoor have been reactivated to amplify disinformation around the ongoing student-led demonstrations over exam paper leaks.
body:
• Delhi Police says approximately 400 Pakistan-linked social media handles, previously flagged during Operation Sindoor, have resurfaced to exploit the ongoing NEET protests
  • The accounts are being identified and blocked in coordination with central cyber agencies, following India's earlier blocking of over 1,400 URLs during the 2025 military operation
  • The claim comes as India's youth-led Cockroach Janta Party movement intensifies pressure on the Modi government over exam paper leaks and education reform

Delhi Police has flagged approximately 400 Pakistan-linked social media handles that it says were originally active during Operation Sindoor and have now been reactivated to target India's expanding NEET protest movement, according to officials familiar with the investigation.

The accounts, which authorities say are being systematically identified and blocked, allegedly seek to amplify discord and spread disinformation amid the largest student-led demonstrations against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government in years.

A Familiar Playbook

The claimed resurgence mirrors tactics documented during Operation Sindoor in May 2025, when India launched retaliatory strikes against Pakistan following the Pahalgam terror attack. The Indian government blocked more than 1,400 URLs on digital platforms during that period, most linked to Pakistan-based accounts circulating "false, misleading, anti-India news content," according to Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw.

https://x.com/NewsAlgebraIND/status/2080353503046959191

"Certain social media handles, many operating from outside India, were actively propagating false and potentially harmful information during Operation Sindoor."

— Ashwini Vaishnaw, Information and Broadcasting Minister

A May 2026 study by the Digital Forensics Research and Analytics Centre (DFRAC) documented a "sustained pattern of misinformation campaigns originating from or amplified by Pakistan-linked social media ecosystems." The research found Pakistan-linked handles circulating domestic protest footage from Bihar and Noida, falsely claiming Indian youth had launched "coordinated anti-government uprisings near military establishments."

The NEET Crisis and CJP Movement

The protests that authorities say are being targeted have grown into a formidable political challenge. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), founded by Boston University graduate Abhijeet Dipke in mid-May 2026, rapidly amassed millions of Instagram followers and organized sustained demonstrations at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar.

On July 20, tens of thousands of protesters attempted to march on Parliament, resulting in clashes that left about 150 protesters and 118 police personnel injured, according to CJP leaders and Delhi Police respectively. Tear gas and baton charges were deployed, and authorities briefly cut internet access in parts of the capital, according to CNN.

The movement demands the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak, which affected approximately two million candidates. About a dozen student suicides have been linked to the exam's cancellation, according to Reuters.

Government's Digital Response

The government's approach has included digital measures that critics say blur the line between counter-disinformation and suppression of dissent. In May, the Intelligence Bureau flagged CJP's own X account as a national security concern, leading to its blocking. The Delhi High Court ordered the account restored on July 7 after the government conceded it no longer objected since the NEET re-exam had concluded.

Pradhan has referred to CJP as the "B-team of terror groups." The International Federation of Journalists warned that "indiscriminate labelling of dissenting voices as 'anti-India' and the subsequent arrests for mere social media posts are deeply troubling."

The claims about Pakistani handle reactivation arrive as opposition leader Rahul Gandhi was briefly detained on July 21 after protesting outside Modi's residence, and the Congress party has vowed to raise the students' cause in Parliament.

What Comes Next

Modi on July 23 announced special courts would be established to prosecute those behind exam paper leaks. CJP rejected the proposal, with spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka asking, "Why are paper leaks happening in this country in the first place?"

Thousands of protesters remain camped at Jantar Mantar. The convergence of genuine student grievances, government counter-disinformation claims, and alleged foreign interference adds layers of complexity to a crisis that shows no signs of abating.
nri_angle: Indian diaspora communities monitoring the protests and government responses are navigating competing narratives online, with foreign disinformation campaigns complicating their ability to assess developments in real time.
